title: Junta Approximation for DNF
statement: There exists a constant $C>0$ such that for every $n,w\in\mathbb N$ and every DNF $d$ on $n$ variables with width at most $w$, and every $0<\varepsilon\le1$, there are a coordinate set $J\subseteq[n]$ and a function $h:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on coordinates in $J$ such that $|J|\le(1/\varepsilon)^{Cw}$ and the uniform probability that $h(x)$ differs from the sign encoding of $d(x)$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: There exists a positive real constant C
n and w are natural numbers
d is a DNF on n variables
The width of d is at most w
replaced: There exists an absolute $C>0$ such that for every DNF $d$ on $n$ variables of width at most $w\in\mathbb N$ and every $0<\varepsilon\le1$, there exist $J\subseteq[n]$ and $h:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on $J$, with $|J|\le(1/\varepsilon)^{Cw}$ and $\Pr_x((-1)^{d(x)}\ne h(x))\le\varepsilon$ under the uniform cube law.
